cells.tense: What is coming in now is already in proportion, and the weight of it reads true.
cells.act: let the old form go so the next one can come
cells.ask: Something here has already run its course, though nothing looks finished. Let it be done this week — no reopening, no going back over it — and leave the space it clears open for whatever is arriving.
cells.core:
What arrives now arrives in proportion. You can feel the weight of a thing and set it level without running the numbers — what's owed and what's given move back and forth without calculation. The fairness doesn't announce itself. In its best version, someone hands you something out of joint and the answer is already there, arriving before any reason, and it holds.

What's entering is carrying an old shape, something that was fair in its season and is only waiting now. Endings go along with this. When an exchange stops being even somewhere, part of you goes quiet so a different thing can start. Give the finished thing its end without reopening it, and the new balance has a place to land instead of a space still occupied. That's not a loss; it's the clearing that makes room.
cells.sheetLine: You feel the weight and set it level without the math.
cells.verb: weighing what is fair and setting it level again
cells.place: the threshold where what is coming in gets met and taken up

cells.tense: What is entering now will be tracked, counted and braced against before it has arrived.
cells.act: bear the next hour of it without deciding anything
cells.ask: When the next thing lands — an offer, a snub, a bill, a kindness — take it the way it comes, without measuring your side against theirs for an hour. Bear that hour and decide nothing. Afterward, you can count.
cells.core:
Fairness, where it's in excess, turns into the ledger. You know what's owed and what you're owed before anyone has done anything — and something entering now gets weighed before it has had a chance to be itself. The tally runs before the moment does. People feel it as a bill, and they aren't wrong: the exchange is running before the exchange exists.

Endurance, not less care, is what settles this. Hold what's coming at its own size. You can take a thing without pricing it, keep your footing without tightening around it, carry a moment without forcing the numbers to balance first. No decision is needed in the first hour it's here. Bearing that load for one hour without a verdict is work that can actually be done, and it's done by staying.
cells.sheetLine: The count starts running before the thing has arrived.
cells.verb: weighing what is fair and setting it level again
cells.place: the threshold where what is coming in gets met and taken up

cells.tense: What was offered before is still what matters, and nothing arriving now gets claimed as yours.
cells.act: do the small practice again, alone, today
cells.ask: Somewhere you accept less than what's fair and call it getting along. The next time you notice it happening — in a chat, a bill, a plan that suits them better — put what you'd actually say on a page, just for yourself.
cells.core:
Where this function is starved, something has been handed over for a long while without being named. A plan gets made that costs you more than it costs others, and you agree. You say it's fine, and part of you means it. The job keeps falling to you; the acknowledgement doesn't. Claiming what's owed doesn't come up as an option.

What's arriving won't change that by itself, so start smaller than the situation. Keep one steady practice that belongs to you alone — a page, a walk, the same ten minutes — and do the plain version of it today, not the plan for it. Refinement comes from repeating a thing by attention. Time by yourself is allowed to connect you, not shut you off from the room; that's what the steady light is for.
cells.sheetLine: You take less than your share and call it keeping the peace.
cells.verb: weighing what is fair and setting it level again
cells.place: the threshold where what is coming in gets met and taken up

cells.tense: You are keeping accounts you don't know you're keeping, and the balance is being written in a room you haven't noticed entering.
cells.act: notice what you already know before you reason about it
cells.ask: There's a score you keep re-checking that you'd deny holding. Don't argue it, don't act on it, and don't decide it's silly — just note it once, quietly, in your own words. Nothing follows.
cells.core:
People can tell you when you've been shorted — days later, and with detail. You don't say you're keeping accounts. You feel things as being out of proportion, and the tally strikes before you'd admit there is one. The record isn't hidden from you; it's that no one, including you, is standing where it's written. Someone is keeping the balance in this corner of your life, and it doesn't feel like you.

Smaller than a reckoning is what actually moves this. What you already have about what's off is usually accurate, and it doesn't need reasons. Notice it once without arguing with it. Let it land and then stop there. Knowing what to attend to doesn't need a case built under it; it needs you to stop talking it out of the room so it can tell you where to look.
cells.sheetLine: The ledger is open. You'd say you didn't open one.
cells.verb: weighing what is fair and setting it level again
cells.place: the threshold where what is coming in gets met and taken up

attempts.check: The unsupported claim is that any of this is arriving as an event outside them — the seat is Ingress on what is entering the person's own life, and I've kept every cell on capacity and moment, not on fate or an external arrival. The reader could reasonably say the tallying is old and personal, not present; each cell describes only the mechanism in a moment they could recognize and leaves history to them. The asks survive being wrong: each is optional, costs nothing, needs no one, and teaches something even if my read misses. The sentence that serves the writer more than the person is 'Fairness flows naturally' — pretty, and it says nothing a person could do, so no cell carries it.
